```{r}

## Load data and samples metadata
metadata <- read.csv(file.path(sampleSheet), sep = ",",stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
passSamples <- read.csv(file.path(groupAnalysisSamples), sep = ",",stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
pheno <- metadata[metadata$sampleID %in% passSamples$sampleID,]

pheno$sequencingBatch <- as.factor(pheno$sequencingBatch)
pheno<- droplevels(pheno)

pheno$fraction[pheno$fraction == "SOX"] <- "SOX10+"
pheno$fraction[pheno$fraction == "NEUN"] <- "NeuN+"
pheno$fraction[pheno$fraction == "IRF8"] <- "IRF8+"

df_ordered <- pheno[order(pheno$fraction), ]
groups <- as.factor(df_ordered$fraction)

```

```{r}

##Functions

## Load counts in peaks files and match to pheno samples data
loadCounts <- function(counts){
  colnames(counts) <- lapply(colnames(counts),function(x) gsub("*.filt.nodup.bam", "",x))
  counts <- counts[, colSums(is.na(counts)) == 0]
  return(counts)
}

## Plot PCA with first two principal components
pca_single <- function(counts,pheno_sub){
  pca <- prcomp(t(counts))
  tpm.scores = pca$x
  tpm.pca<-pca$sdev^2/sum(pca$sdev^2)
  tpm.scores<-tpm.scores[,which(tpm.pca > 0.01)]
  percentVar = round(100 * (tpm.pca) )
  tpm.scores.df = cbind(pc1 = tpm.scores[,1],pc2 = tpm.scores[,2],
                        pc3 = tpm.scores[,3],pc4 = tpm.scores[,4]
                        ,pheno_sub)
  plot1 <- ggplot(tpm.scores.df, aes(x=pc1, y=pc2, color = fraction,label= sampleCode))+
    geom_point(size=2, alpha = 0.7)+
    labs(x=paste0("PC1 (", percentVar[1], "%)"),y=paste0("PC2 (", percentVar[2], "%)"),  
         title = "", color = "Cell type") +
    scale_color_manual(values = col_vals_plots) +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(
      legend.position = "bottom",legend.key.size = unit(1.3, 'cm'),
      legend.text = element_text(size =12),legend.title = element_text(size = 12),
      axis.title = element_text(margin = margin(r = 15), size = 12),
      axis.text = element_text(size =12), 
    )+ guides(shape = guide_legend(nrow = 2))
  
  return(plot1)
}

## Plot PCA with first four principal components
pca_multiple <- function(counts,pheno_sub){
  pca <- prcomp(t(counts))
  tpm.scores = pca$x
  tpm.pca<-pca$sdev^2/sum(pca$sdev^2)
  tpm.scores<-tpm.scores[,which(tpm.pca > 0.01)]
  percentVar = round(100 * (tpm.pca) )
  tpm.scores.df <- data.frame(pc1 = tpm.scores[,1],pc2 = tpm.scores[,2], pc3 = tpm.scores[,3],pc4 = tpm.scores[,4],fraction = as.factor(pheno_sub$fraction), cohort = as.factor(pheno_sub$cohort),sampleCode =as.factor(pheno_sub$sampleCode), gender =as.factor(pheno_sub$"gender") )

  plot1 <- ggplot(tpm.scores.df, aes(x=pc1, y=pc2, color = fraction))+geom_point(size=2)+ theme_bw()+
    labs(x=paste0("PC1: ", percentVar[1], "% variance"),y=paste0("PC2: ", percentVar[2], "% variance")) +theme(legend.position="none")+ scale_color_manual(values = col_vals_plots)
  
  plot2 <- ggplot(tpm.scores.df, aes(x=pc3, y=pc4, color = fraction)) + geom_point(size=2)+theme_bw() +
    labs(x=paste0("PC3: ", percentVar[3], "% variance"),y=paste0("PC4: ", percentVar[4], "% variance")) +theme(legend.position="right")+ scale_color_manual(values = col_vals_plots)
  
  plot3 <- ggplot(tpm.scores.df, aes(x=pc1, y=pc4, color = fraction)) + geom_point(size=2)+theme_bw() +
    labs(x=paste0("PC1: ", percentVar[1], "% variance"),y=paste0("PC4: ", percentVar[4], "% variance")) +theme(legend.position="none")+ scale_color_manual(values = col_vals_plots)
  plot4 <- ggplot(tpm.scores.df, aes(x=pc1, y=pc3, color = fraction)) + geom_point(size=2)+theme_bw() +
    labs(x=paste0("PC1: ", percentVar[1], "% variance"),y=paste0("PC3: ", percentVar[3], "% variance")) +theme(legend.position="none")+ scale_color_manual(values = col_vals_plots)
  
  figure <- ggarrange(plot1,plot2,plot3,plot4,labels = c("A", "B", "C","D"),ncol = 2, nrow=2)   
  return(figure)
}

## Calculate PCA scores for silhouette score
pca_transform <- function(data){
  pca <- prcomp(t(data), center = TRUE, scale. = FALSE)
  
  var_explained <- pca$sdev^2 / sum(pca$sdev^2)
  cum_var <- cumsum(var_explained)
  pc_scores <- pca$x[, c(1:5)]
  return(pc_scores)
}

## Calculate mean silhouette coefficient
calc.sil <- function(data, group_labels) {
  
  # Check if data is a matrix or data frame and convert if necessary
  if (!is.matrix(data)) data <- as.matrix(data)
  d <- dist(data)  # Euclidean distance in PC space
  sil <- silhouette(as.integer(as.factor(group_labels)), d)
  
  results <- data.frame(
    sample = rownames(data),
    assigned_cluster = group_labels,
    cluster_number = sil[, "cluster"],
    neighbor_cluster = sil[, "neighbor"],
    sil_width = sil[, "sil_width"]
  )
  
  return(results)
}

## PCA plot with failed samples marked
pca_qcs3 <- function(counts,pheno_sub){
  pca <- prcomp(t(counts))
  tpm.scores = pca$x
  tpm.pca<-pca$sdev^2/sum(pca$sdev^2)
  tpm.scores<-tpm.scores[,which(tpm.pca > 0.01)]
  percentVar = round(100 * (tpm.pca) )
  tpm.scores.df <- data.frame(pc1 = tpm.scores[,1],pc2 = tpm.scores[,2],
                              fraction = as.factor(pheno_sub$fraction),
                              cohort = as.factor(pheno_sub$cohort),
                              sampleCode =as.factor(pheno_sub$sampleCode), 
                              sampleID =as.factor(pheno_sub$sampleID), 
                              gender =as.factor(pheno_sub$gender), passed = pheno_sub$QCS3)
  
  plot1 <- ggplot(tpm.scores.df, aes(x=pc1, y=pc2, color =  fraction,
                                     shape = passed, label = sampleCode))+
    geom_point(size=2, alpha = 0.7)+
  scale_shape_manual(values = c("FALSE" = 3, "TRUE" = 16)) + 
    scale_color_manual(values = col_vals_plots) +
    labs(x=paste0("PC1: ", percentVar[1], "% variance"),
         y=paste0("PC2: ", percentVar[2], "% variance"), 
         color = "Cell-type", 
         title    = paste0("Cell-type check: PCA of top ",diffN, " cell differential ATAC peaks"),
         subtitle = "Outliers defined by negative silhouette coefficient", 
         shape = "Pass QC Stage 3") +
    theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
    theme(
      legend.position = "bottom",legend.key.size = unit(1.3, 'cm'),
      legend.text = element_text(size =12),legend.title = element_text(size = 12),
      axis.title = element_text(margin = margin(r = 15), size = 12),
      axis.text = element_text(size =12), 
    )+ guides(shape = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size=6),ncol = 1),
              colour = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size=6),ncol = 2))
  
  return(plot1)
}
```

## Overview

This is the third stage of PIPPA. After having check the quality and identity of samples, this third stage checks for the assigned cell type of the samples, as well as to identify samples where sorting might have not fully worked. To do this, we will perform a cell type check using the read counts in peaks called at cell type level.

In total, `r nrow(metadata)` were profiled and `r nrow(passSamples)` samples passed stage 1 (data quality) and 2 (identity) check of the QC. Below, the number of samples used to perform peak calling at cell type level is shown. Peak calling was performed using MACS3 in paired-end mode.

```{r}
nCTStart<-table(metadata$fraction)
nCTMid<-table(passSamples$fraction)
ctCounts<-cbind(nCTStart, nCTMid)
colnames(ctCounts)<-c("Profiled", "Samples for Peak Calling")
kbl(ctCounts) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"),font_size = 10)

```

## 1.Raw counts

First, we will explore the raw read counts in peaks. 

```{r}
load(groupCountsAll)
counts.raw <- loadCounts(fc_ctPeaks$counts)
cnt_table <- fc_ctPeaks$annotation

#filter and align metadata
pheno.filt <- pheno[pheno$sampleID %in% colnames(counts.raw),]
pheno.filt <- pheno.filt[match(colnames(counts.raw),pheno.filt$sampleID),]
stopifnot(all(colnames(counts.raw) == pheno.filt$sampleID))

```

The total number of counts in peaks is `r nrow(counts)` and `r ncol(counts)` samples, `r dim(counts)` is dimension of counts and `r dim(pheno.filt)` the sample sheet. In order to reduce noise, peaks with low counts are filtered out. The number of peaks filtered is shown below.

```{r}
counts.dge <- DGEList(counts=counts.raw, samples=pheno.filt)
keep <- filterByExpr(counts.dge, group = pheno.filt$fraction)
counts.dge.filt <- counts.dge[keep,]

print(nrow(counts.raw)-nrow(counts.dge.filt))
```

## 2.Normalised counts in peaks

Normalisation is applied to raw counts in peaks to account for biases or factors that we are not interested in. The expression levels of samples become more comparable between and/or within samples.

### 2.1 Variance Stabilizing Transformation (VST)

VST is first used to transform the counts data. This selects `r diffN` peaks that are 'representative' of the dataset's dispersion trend, and uses the information from these to perform the transformation. The two first PCAs of the transformed data is shown below. The filtered set of counts in peaks is used here.

```{r}
dds.filt <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(countData = counts.dge.filt,
                                   colData = pheno.filt,
                                   design = ~ fraction)

## normalise counts in peaks with VST transform
vst <- vst(dds.filt)
counts.norm <- assay(vst)

ggplotly(pca_single(counts.norm, pheno.filt))
```

## 3. Cell-type check

The main goal of this third part of the pipeline is to check the cell-type assigned to each sample. The counts in cell-type peaks can be used for this, as we will check the clustering of samples based on this. For this, we have perform differential analysis between the cell-groups of samples to obtain the peaks that differentiates the cell-types. The top `r diffN` differential peaks are used for the clustering of samples and the identification of potential mislabeled samples.

```{r}
load(diffPeaksCountsAll)
res_sorted <- results[order(results$FDR, decreasing = FALSE),]
most_significant_peaks <- rownames(head(res_sorted, diffN))
counts.dif <- counts.norm[most_significant_peaks,]
counts_to_plot <- counts.dif
```

### 3.1 Clustering of samples

#### Principal component analysis

We perform PCA to investigate the clustering of samples based on cell-types for the top `r diffN` differential peaks.

```{r}
ggplotly(pca_single(counts_to_plot, pheno.filt))
```

We can also explore multiple PCs.
```{r fig.height = 8, fig.width = 8} 

pca_multiple(counts_to_plot, pheno.filt)
```

```{r fig.height = 8, fig.width = 8} 
rownames(pheno.filt) <- pheno.filt$sampleID
p <- PCAtools::pca(counts_to_plot, metadata = pheno.filt)
pca_plot <- PCAtools::pairsplot(p, colby = "fraction",components = c(1:10),
                         colkey= col_vals_plots,pointSize = 1)

pdf(file.path(paste0(peakDir, "/QCOutput/10PCs.pdf")), width = 20, height = 20)
pca_plot
dev.off()
```

#### Hierarchical clustering

We use hierarchical clustering to cluster samples based on counts in peaks (top `r diffN`) and identify groups of samples based on cell-types, sequencing batch or cohort.

```{r ,fig.height = 20, fig.width = 20}

cm = data.frame(as.matrix(counts_to_plot))
pheno.filt$sequencingBatch <- as.factor(pheno.filt$sequencingBatch)
anno = as.data.frame(pheno.filt[,c("fraction", "sequencingBatch", "cohort", "gender")])
rownames(anno) <- pheno.filt$sampleCode
colnames(cm) = rownames(anno)
colnames(anno)<-c("Cell Fraction", "sequencingBatch", "cohort","gender")
rownames(cm) = NULL
my_palette <- colorRampPalette(c("blue", "white", "red"))(50)
breaks <- seq(-2, 2, length.out = 51)
annotation_colors <- list("Cell Fraction" = col_vals_plots)

pheatmap(cm, annotation_col = anno,cluster_cols=TRUE,color = my_palette, annotation_colors  = annotation_colors,cluster_rows=FALSE,scale="row",show_rownames=FALSE,show_colnames = FALSE,fontsize_col = 2,cutree_cols = 4,breaks = breaks)
```

#### Sample-to-Sample distance

The distance between samples is an additional method to evaluate the similarity between samples within and between cell-fraction groups.

```{r ,fig.height = 20, fig.width = 20}
cm = data.frame(as.matrix(counts_to_plot))
anno = as.data.frame(pheno.filt[,c("fraction","gender", "sequencingBatch", "cohort")])
rownames(anno) <- pheno.filt$sampleCode
colnames(cm) = rownames(anno)
colnames(anno)<-c("Cell Fraction","gender", "sequencingBatch", "cohort")
my_palette <- colorRampPalette(c("blue", "white", "red"))(50)
annotation_colors <- list("Cell Fraction" = col_vals_plots)

sampleDists <- dist(t(cm))
sampleDistMatrix <- as.matrix(sampleDists)
p <-pheatmap(sampleDistMatrix,
        clustering_distance_rows = sampleDists,
       clustering_distance_cols = sampleDists,
         col = my_palette ,annotation_colors  = annotation_colors,annotation_col=anno,fontsize_col = 2, fontsize_row = 2)
p
pdf(file.path(paste0(peakDir, "/QCOutput/sampleToSampleDist.pdf")), width = 15, height = 15)
print(p)
dev.off()
```

## 4. Silhouette score

The silhouette coefficient (or silhouette score) is a metric used to evaluate the quality of clustering in a dataset. It provides a measure of how similar each point in one cluster is to points in the same cluster compared to points in other clusters. 

- *High score* (close to 1): The sample is well matched to its own cluster and poorly matched to neighboring clusters.
- *Low score* (close to 0): The sample is on or very close to the boundary between clusters.
- *Negative score* (close to −1): The sample is assigned to the wrong cluster.

We use the VST transform counts in peaks to calculate the silhouette coefficient and identify samples that are not in the right cell-type group or that do not cluster with their group. Samples that have a silhouette score below `r silScore` will be failed.

```{r}
counts_to_plot.s <- pca_transform(counts_to_plot)
counts.silh.norm<- calc.sil(counts_to_plot.s,pheno.filt$fraction)
```

### 4.1 Mark failed samples

We use the first two PCAs to cluster samples based on their assigned cell-types and those that have failed based on the silhouette score threshold are marked with a X.

Below there is a table of number of samples that failed stage 3 of QC, so that their labelled cell-type might be wrong.

```{r fig.height = 6, fig.width = 8} 
counts.silh.norm <- counts.silh.norm[match(pheno.filt$sampleID,counts.silh.norm$sample),]
pheno.filt$QCS3 <- ifelse(counts.silh.norm$sil_width > silScore, "TRUE", "FALSE")

counts <- as.data.frame(table(pheno.filt$QCS3))
names(counts) <- c("Pass Cell-type check", "Count")

knitr::kable(counts)
```

#### Principal component analysis

```{r fig.height = 8, fig.width = 8} 
ggplotly(pca_qcs3(counts_to_plot,pheno.filt),tooltip="label")
```

```{r fig.height = 10, fig.width = 8} 
pheno.filt$QCS3 <- as.factor(pheno.filt$QCS3)
rownames(pheno.filt) <- pheno.filt$sampleID
p <- PCAtools::pca(counts_to_plot, metadata = pheno.filt)
pca_plot <- PCAtools::pairsplot(p, colby = "fraction",components = c(1:5),
                         colkey= col_vals_plots,pointSize = 1, shape ="QCS3",
                         shapekey = c("FALSE" = 3, "TRUE" = 16))

pca_plot
```

Below, samples that fail at this third QC stage are shown.

```{r}

wrongCT <- pheno.filt[pheno.filt$QCS3==FALSE,]
counts <- as.data.frame(table(wrongCT$fraction))
names(counts) <- c("Failed cell-type check", "Count")

knitr::kable(counts)
```

## Collate results from previous Stage 1 and 2, and new Stage 3 results in a single table

allQC <- metadata
qc1 <- read.csv(file.path(qc1pass), sep = ",",stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
qc1$QCPASS <- as.factor(qc1$QCPASS)

## Collate results from previous Stage 1 and 2, and new Stage 3 results in a single table
